You talk to the Special Forces recruiter on post, pass the PT test, get your commander to sign your packet, and get a slot at Special Forces Assessment and Selection (SFAS) at Camp Mackall, North Carolina.
You walk across the stage at Fort Bragg and put on the green beret for the first time.
Day 4. Night land nav, alone, with a map, compass and 50 pounds on your back. No GPS, no lights. The "Star Course" points are spread across miles of North Carolina swamp.
Shoot a careful azimuth and count paces
You found every point with time to spare.
You missed a point by a few hundred meters and ran out of time.
Use the road to move faster
You moved fast on the road and nobody caught you.
Cadre caught you on a road. Instant drop for "road walking."
Your team has to move a jeep frame full of sandbags 12 miles. Nobody tells you how you are doing. The cadre just watch and write in their notebooks.
Lead quietly and carry more than your share
The cadre wrote something down after watching you carry two sandbags at once.
You burned yourself out and fell behind.
Your team followed you. It worked, barely.
Peers rated you as a bad teammate in the peer reviews.
Ruck march with no known distance. When you think you're finished, they tell you to keep going.
You kept going without a word. That's the point of the event.
Your feet gave out with blisters down to the meat.
Keep moving, candidate. You kept going.
The cadre noted it. Selection boards hate quitters' questions.

He didn't trust you and your mission fell apart.
Push him to follow your plan

You earn the tan beret and the 75th Ranger Regiment scroll.
Smoke sessions at all hours. The cadre want to see who quits before the real training starts.
You made it through the first week. Dozens didn't.
You fell out of a run and got recycled.
Complain to the guy next to you

12 miles with a heavy ruck in under three hours.
You finished with minutes to spare.
You missed the time hack by two minutes.

Recognizing that I volunteered as a Ranger... You nailed every word.
You blanked on the fourth stanza.
Sixty-one days of patrols across Fort Benning, the mountains of Georgia and the Florida swamps. One meal a day, a few hours of sleep.
Your patrol hit the objective on time. GO.

You pin on the gold Trident. You're a Navy SEAL.
